title: HPV vaccine
what: A vaccine shot in the upper arm. It protects against human papillomavirus, which can cause cervical cancer and other diseases.
why: Best for children aged about 9 to 14, before they become sexually active. For teens and adults, on a doctor's advice.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes; the course is 1 to 3 shots, depending on age
tell_doctor: If you are ill now or have a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines
If you have fainted from shots before

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are well. You will have a short check first.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Best to eat beforehand. Teens feel dizzy more often on an empty stomach.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: Your doctor will say how many shots are needed and how far apart. Check with the clinic.

steps: The doctor asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped, and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in your documents
After the shot, sit in the clinic for 15 to 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes soreness or redness at the spot for 1 to 3 days
Sometimes tiredness, a headache, or a mild fever
after: Stay near the room, and do not stand up suddenly
You can go back to normal activities
Next shot on schedule, if needed
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services
Fainting after the shot: lay the person down and call the nurse

faq.q: Why vaccinate a child so early?
faq.a: The vaccine works best before contact with the virus. Children's immune systems respond more strongly.
In many countries, it is recommended for boys too. Ask your doctor.

faq.q: Does the vaccine replace gynecology checkups?
faq.a: No. Regular checkups and smear tests are still needed.

reminders.text: HPV vaccine tomorrow. Have breakfast in the morning, and bring your vaccination record.
